rows.selection_reason: Existing evidence is sparse, so the first experiment should test a balanced multimodal configuration with moderate complexity. config_001 uses PCA (simple RNA encoding) and ResNet50 (standard image encoder) with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion, which are computationally efficient. This clarifies the baseline performance of a standard multimodal setup, balancing exploration of key components (multimodal, multiprofile) with manageable training cost (estimated ~5 GPU hours).

Existing evidence shows config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, pca_n2000 RNA, resnet50 image, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.639 accuracy. This experiment tests replacing resnet50 with imagenet_vit_l (a more complex image encoder) while keeping other components identical. This clarifies whether the image encoder choice significantly impacts performance. The expected cost is higher than config_001 (likely ~12-15 GPU hours) but offers potential for improvement, balancing exploration of critical design choices with exploitation of similar architecture.

Existing evidence shows multimodal models with pca_n2000 RNA and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (config_006) achieve 0.635 accuracy at 7.02 GPU hours, while config_001 (same RNA but resnet50 image) has slightly higher accuracy (0.639) at higher cost. This experiment tests transformer aggregation and concat fusion (vs avgpool+weighted in previous configs), which could improve performance. It uses the same image encoder as config_006 but with more complex aggregation/fusion, offering a promising balance between exploration and cost (estimated ~8-9 GPU hours).

The existing evidence shows that multimodal configurations with avgpool aggregation and weighted fusion (like config_001) achieve the highest accuracy so far (0.639). This experiment tests using a more complex RNA encoder (scvi_n200) and image encoder (imagenet_vit_l) while retaining the effective aggregation/fusion strategy. It clarifies whether upgrading both encoders improves accuracy without excessive cost. The expected cost is moderate (~12 GPU hours), balancing exploration of encoder improvements with budget constraints.

The existing evidence shows config_018 (0.7062 accuracy) is the best so far with low cost. This experiment tests whether switching the image encoder from imagenet_vit_l to resnet50 (used in config_001) maintains high accuracy while potentially reducing cost. It clarifies if the image encoder choice is critical, and offers a cheaper alternative if accuracy remains high. Expected cost: ~7.0 GPU hours.

The existing evidence shows config_018 (0.706245 accuracy) is the best so far using scvi_n200 RNA, imagenet_vit_l image, avgpool, and weighted fusion. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation (more complex) while keeping other components the same, which could improve accuracy. The expected cost is ~5.5 GPU hours (moderate increase from 4.82), balancing exploitation of the current best setup with exploration of aggregation methods. This clarifies if transformer aggregation benefits this high-performing configuration.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (e.g., config_024) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with the same image encoder and fusion method, exploring if a different RNA encoder could improve accuracy. It balances exploitation of proven components (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted fusion) with exploration of a new RNA encoder (scgpt), which may offer better performance. The expected cost is similar to config_024 (3.60 GPU hours) due to comparable model complexity.

The existing evidence shows that configurations using scvi_n200 RNA encoder and imagenet_vit_l image encoder (e.g., config_024) achieve high accuracy. This experiment tests config_022, which uses scvi_n200 and resnet50 image encoder with transformer aggregation and concat fusion. It clarifies whether switching the image encoder to resnet50 (which is less expensive) and changing the fusion method could maintain high accuracy while reducing cost. This balances exploitation of current top performers with exploration of cost-effective alternatives.

Existing evidence shows that using scvi_n200 RNA encoder with transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_024) achieves high accuracy. This experiment tests the same RNA and image encoders but with concat fusion, clarifying if fusion method impacts performance. It balances exploration of key design choices (fusion) with cost-effectiveness, as transformer aggregation and resnet50 are already supported by prior results.

Existing evidence shows that models using scvi_n200 RNA encoder, imagenet_vit_l image encoder, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_024) achieve the highest accuracy (0.725). This experiment tests whether substituting resnet50 for imagenet_vit_l (a smaller image encoder) with pca_n2000 RNA encoder maintains performance. It clarifies if the image encoder's complexity or RNA encoder type is more critical. This is the best use of the last experiment as it directly compares to the current top-performing configuration, with an estimated cost of 4.5 GPU hours.
